citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the SVD-entropy and Petrosian cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::katzFD: Katz's fractal dimension in the amplitude-only convention = log10(L/a)/log10(d/a), L=sum|dx|, a=mean|dx|, d=max|x-x0|. The reference re-computes it with BOTH antropy.katz_fd and NeuroKit2 fractal_katz, via reticulate, and also computes the earlier Euclidean-plane convention for the difference metric. Deterministic.
note: katzFD is a NEW standalone op that completes the fractal-dimension family in PhysioEEG (petrosianFD, svdEntropy); Katz FD previously existed only inside eegComplexity. It reproduces BOTH antropy.katz_fd AND NeuroKit2 fractal_katz BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0 vs each) -- a double-reference agreement, because the amplitude-only closed form is identical in all three. INTEGRITY FIX: the two dominant Python references (antropy, NeuroKit2), plus pyeeg and mne-features, all measure the distances in the signal's AMPLITUDE units only, even though their docstrings say 'Euclidean'; the shipped eegComplexity(measure='katz_fd') previously used the TRUE Euclidean distance in the sample-index/amplitude plane, which mixes the axes' units, is scale-dependent, and matches no reference (KFD 1.696 vs the field-standard 3.468 here). This fold adopts the amplitude-only convention for both the new op and the eegComplexity path, restoring cross-tool comparability. Note the amplitude-only KFD is not bounded to [1,2] (it scales with the amplitude-to-step ratio), which is why real EEG yields values above 2 -- this matches what antropy/NeuroKit2 return.
